item.description:
**A terminal keeps 10,000 lines of history.** It kept 500 — SwiftTerm's own default — so a log or a long build scrolled out of reach within a few screens, and Find could only search what was left. Raising it waited on something else: every ssh session read its whole screen five times a second, history and all, to watch for a host-key question, which already cost a session up to 6% of the main thread at 500 lines and would have cost far more at 10,000. A session now reads its screen only while it is connecting, while a question is up, and for two minutes after it comes through, which covers every hop of a jump chain. After that, a host-key question asked by something you run inside the session — an `ssh` typed there, `git` over ssh — is answered in the terminal itself, as in Terminal.app, rather than through Shellhand's dialog.
**Shellhand asks a host what it runs only while you let it.** Asking is a second login, once a day per host, and on a machine with login alerts or a session recorder that is something somebody sees. Settings ▸ General has a Hosts section now, with a switch that turns the asking off. It starts on, as asking always has, and turning it off keeps the marks already learned.
**Report a Problem opens a form.** Help ▸ Report a Problem… opens a new issue on a form that asks what happened and what you expected, with the versions of Shellhand and macOS already filled in. Questions and ideas have a place of their own now, in the repository's Discussions.
**A settings file Shellhand cannot use says so now, and so does an import.** A mistake in `config.yaml` — an unclosed quote, a setting spelled wrong, an option ssh would refuse — left Shellhand running without the file, its ssh options and palettes quietly not applied, and a YAML import with a mistake in it came in as an empty list. Neither said a word, in any release so far. Now the window says what is wrong with the settings file when it opens, the import refuses the file with its reason, and a YAML mistake comes with its line and column. The settings file is read when Shellhand opens, so a fix takes effect the next time it does.
Nothing else here is visible from the outside. The suite went from 622 checks to 643, the history's size was measured before it was chosen — about 8 bytes a column for each line, so 8 to 16 MB a session at 10,000 lines — and the settings file's message was checked on screen, against a copy of the app with a broken file of its own.

**Quick Connect reaches machines that are not in your list.** Type `user@host:port` into ⌘K — or `host`, `host:port`, `[v6]:port`, or paste an `ssh://` link — and the palette offers to connect to it as typed, under "Not in your list". A host you have saved still comes first when what you typed names it exactly, so its key and its jump host still apply; an address, or a destination with a user or a port, comes next, ahead of saved hosts that merely contain it; and a bare word is still a search, its own row last. Nothing typed this way is saved, and ⌘R and ⌘T work on it like on any other session.
**The tabs answer the keys every other Mac app gives them.** ⇧⌘] and ⇧⌘[ move to the next and the previous tab, and so do ⌃⇥ and ⌃⇧⇥, going round from the last to the first and taking in the Hosts tab on the way. ⌘T opens another session like the one in front — to the same machine, or another local shell — where it used to open whatever the list had selected, which need not have been the machine you were looking at. With the Hosts tab in front it still opens the host selected.
**A tab has a menu of its own.** Right-click one for Reconnect, Duplicate, SFTP, Close Tab and Close Other Tabs, each acting on the tab you clicked rather than the one in front. Reconnecting or closing a session that is still running asks first, exactly as ⌘R and ⌘W do, and closing the others asks once for all of them.
**The terminal's font is yours to choose.** Settings ▸ Terminal has a Font picker now: SF Mono, as before, or any monospaced font installed — a Nerd Font for a prompt that draws its own glyphs included — with a line of sample text drawn in it, so it is chosen by looking. Open sessions change at once and keep the size they are at, and Actual Size keeps the font rather than going back to SF Mono. A font that is no longer installed falls back to SF Mono rather than leaving a terminal in one it cannot draw.
**⌥⌘K clears the scrollback.** Clear Scrollback, in the Terminal menu, drops everything above the screen and keeps what is on it — vim or less in front included — on the key Terminal.app gives it. ⌘K stays Quick Connect.
**Export and Help are where you would look for them.** File ▸ Export… writes your list as YAML, where it used to be found only inside the Import window. The Help menu opens the README, and Report a Problem… opens a new issue already holding the version and the macOS it came from — and nothing else.
**The host panel no longer breaks an address in two.** The line saying where a host goes — `deploy@203.0.113.21 port 2222` — sat beside Edit and Connect in whatever room they left, and wrapped inside the address. It has a full line of its own now, and one too long even for that is shortened in the middle, whole on its tooltip.
Nothing else here is visible from the outside. The suite went from 570 checks to 622, and the tab keys were also pressed on a copy of the app on screen, each moving the tab in front.

**A host is drawn with the mark of the system it runs.** The first time you connect to a machine, Shellhand asks it what it is — by reading its own `/etc/os-release` over a connection of its own, rather than guessing from what it says when you log in — and from then on the host carries that distribution's mark in the list, the cards and the sidebar: Ubuntu, Debian, Fedora, Alpine, Arch, NixOS and two dozen more. Hover over one and it names the system in words, and the panel on the right says so on a row of its own. Asking is a login of its own, so a machine is asked once a day rather than on every connect, which is also how one rebuilt onto something else corrects itself. A machine that cannot say — one reached only with a password, or with no such file — keeps the plain icon.
**What your ssh config does to a host is shown rather than left for you to work out.** A host whose name matches a `Host` entry in your `~/.ssh/config` that points at a different machine is flagged, since the settings written there are not this host's. A host your config sends through a bastion shows that jump host instead of a dash, and one it reaches through a `ProxyCommand` shows the command on a row of its own. And where a host's name matches an entry for the same machine, connecting now uses that name, so the settings written under it apply — exactly as they do when you type `ssh` with that name yourself. Most of this was built in earlier releases and never switched on: nothing handed it your config.
**An ssh config that includes itself could hold the app up for a minute or more.** A config that pulls in a folder of files, one of which includes that same folder again — an easy line to copy — was read over and over, on the welcome screen and on every import. Each file is read once now, and the same config takes a moment.
**Option types what your keyboard puts on it.** Option was always treated as Meta, so ⌥ and a key sent Escape and the bare key — and on the many layouts outside the US that put `@`, `|`, `{}` or `[]` on Option, those could not be typed into a session at all. It types the character now, as Terminal.app does. If you use Option to move by word in the shell — ⌥B, ⌥F — turn on **Use Option as Meta key** in Settings ▸ Terminal; sessions already open change at once.
**Closing a live session asks first, as Settings always said it did.** "Ask before closing a live session" has been a switch in Settings since the first release, and nothing ever read it: ⌘W, a tab's ×, the window's close button and ⌘Q all ended sessions that were still running, without a word. Each of them asks now, and so does ⌘R, since reconnecting a session that is still up ends it first; quitting counts the sessions in every window. A session still connecting, or one that has already ended, closes without a question, and the switch in Settings ▸ General still turns all of it off.
**A terminal's colours are chosen by looking at them.** The panel on the right has a Colours row now, and it opens every palette drawn as a small terminal in its own colours — because "Gruvbox Dark" and "Tomorrow Night" are both dark and neither name says which is warm. A choice applies to that host's open tabs at once and the list stays up, so two can be compared on the terminal behind it. Settings draws its palette the same way, in place of the chart of sixteen colours it used to show. And the terminal's text sits a little in from the edges now, with its background still running all the way to them.
**On a fresh install, New Local Shell opened a shell you could not see.** With no hosts in the list yet, the welcome took the whole window, so a local shell started behind it — running, with no tab and nothing on screen to show it was there. The welcome stands in only for the host list now, and the shell comes up in a tab like any other.
Nothing else here is visible from the outside. The suite went from 495 checks to 570, and each closing question above was also checked on screen, against a copy of the app with a host list of its own: every one came up in its own words, and Cancel left everything open.
